interviewQuestions.question: When would you NOT use serverless?
interviewQuestions.answerMarkdown:
⭐ **Q: When would you NOT use serverless?**

Two failure shapes. Cost: for steady, high, round-the-clock traffic, the per-invocation premium is paid on every request with no idle time to save on — a flat-rate VM usually wins. Execution shape: genuinely long-running or stateful work — a 30-minute transcode, a persistent WebSocket — fights the execution-time limits and stateless model rather than fitting them.

I'd also flag vendor lock-in from provider-specific triggers, and harder debugging with no long-lived process to attach to. I'd model the cost crossover before deciding.

**Testing:** whether you can name real failure modes with reasoning, not just "it depends."
